prompt: Some people think that older and more experienced employees are useful for a company. Others feel that modern younger employees are better for an organisation. do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Some people lean towards hiring older, experienced employees to avoid costly mistakes, while others prefer younger employees for their knowledge of new technology. In my view, both groups are valuable, since a company benefits from experience as well as fresh technical skills.

When someone applies for a job, one of the first things employers ask about is their previous work experience. This shows how highly experience is valued in the workplace, and some companies will not even consider candidates who do not have it, regardless of their qualifications. Experience might help avoid costly mistakes and reduces the risk involved in important decisions. For example, many companies promote someone who already has experience within the company to a managerial role. That saves the company a significant amount of time and money, since someone who has experience usually already knows the clients, system and most importantly the staff.

However, younger employees bring skills that many experienced staff lack, particularly with new technology. Having grown up with smartphones and the internet, they often adapt to new software far more quickly than older colleagues. They are also more likely to suggest fresh ideas, since they are not attached to the way things have always been done. This matters because companies that target younger consumers depend on staff who understand them, and younger employees are often best placed to do so.

In conclusion, I believe both older and younger employees are valuable. Experience helps companies avoid costly mistakes, while younger workers keep them up to date with new technology, so the most successful organisations employ a mix of both.
